_notes: One Sora 2 Pro prompt per lesson. ~20 second 16:9 720p educational videos with synchronized voiceover and on-screen text. Filenames: web/public/lesson-videos/<lessonId>.mp4. Each prompt follows a structured scene-by-scene script with voiceover lines, on-screen titles, and a strong negative prompt to keep behavior safe and Florida-accurate.
_globalNegative: No accidents, no crashes, no honking, no aggressive driving, no police sirens at night, no rain, no nighttime, no cluttered city traffic, no extra pedestrians, no bicycles, no emergency vehicles unless explicitly required, no confusing road layouts, no cars rolling through stop signs, no unreadable signs, no unsafe behavior, no jaywalking, no children running into the road, no alcohol, no drinks, no phone use while driving, no readable garbled text, no misspelled words, no Florida license plates with personal info, no logos.
_globalStyle: Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic but simple. Camera: smooth, with clear overhead views when explaining right of way. Mood: calm, safe, easy for a new driver to understand. Aspect 16:9. All text on screen must be in clean sans-serif, large, perfectly spelled. Voiceover is calm, friendly, confident American English.

lessons.car-l1-signs:
Create a realistic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching how SIGN SHAPE and COLOR communicate the rule before you can read the words. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic but simple, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm friendly American English instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Smooth aerial pan across a sunny Florida suburban street with palm trees, then cut to a row of standard MUTCD highway signs floating cleanly against a soft white background: a red octagonal STOP sign, a red-and-white triangular YIELD sign, a yellow diamond CURVE warning sign, an orange diamond construction sign, a pentagonal yellow-green SCHOOL ZONE sign. Title text fades in centered: 'Sign Shapes & Colors'. Voiceover: 'Before you read the words, the shape and color of a sign tell you what's coming.'

0:04–0:09 STOP: Camera pushes in on the red octagonal STOP sign. Big on-screen text appears beside it: 'OCTAGON = STOP. Always come to a complete stop.' Voiceover: 'Only one shape in America is an octagon — the stop sign. Always come to a complete stop.'

0:09–0:13 YIELD: Camera slides to the red-and-white triangle. On-screen text: 'TRIANGLE = YIELD. Slow down and give right of way.' Voiceover: 'A downward triangle means yield. Slow down and let other traffic go first.'

0:13–0:17 WARNING: Camera slides to the yellow diamond. On-screen text: 'YELLOW DIAMOND = WARNING. A hazard is ahead.' Voiceover: 'A yellow diamond warns you a hazard is coming, like a curve, school, or signal.'

0:17–0:20 CLOSING CARD: All five signs tile back together with the recap text: 'Shape and color tell you what to do — even before you read the words.' Voiceover closes: 'Learn the shapes and colors. They tell you what to do, every time.'

Visual rules: signs are MUTCD-faithful, perfectly spelled, large and crisp. No cars actually moving in this clip — it is a clean instructional sign-board video. No people, no pedestrians.

Negative prompt: no misspelled signs, no purple or pink signs, no fictional sign shapes, no clutter, no logos, no readable secondary text other than the sign legends and the captions specified above, no accidents, no aggressive driving.
lessons.car-l2-row:
Create a realistic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching the rule for a 4-WAY STOP. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, calm suburban street, smooth cinematic camera with clear overhead views, 16:9.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide overhead view of a clean suburban 4-way intersection with red STOP signs on every corner and visible white stop lines. Title fades in: '4-Way Stop'. Subtitle: 'First to arrive, first to go.' Voiceover: 'At a four-way stop, the rule is simple: first to arrive, first to go.'

0:04–0:11 ORDER OF ARRIVAL: A blue car arrives from the south and stops fully behind the white line. A small floating label '1st' appears above it. Two seconds later a yellow car stops on the west side, label '2nd'. Two seconds later a gray car stops on the north side, label '3rd'. On-screen text: 'Whoever stops first goes first.' A green arrow appears above the blue car and the blue car drives straight through; the others stay still. Voiceover: 'Every driver must come to a complete stop. The car that stops first goes first.'

0:11–0:16 SAME TIME: Cut to the same intersection reset. A blue car from the south and a red car from the east arrive and stop at the EXACT same moment. Both cars get a clean highlight ring. On-screen text: 'Same time? The car on the RIGHT goes first.' Voiceover: 'If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right has the right of way.'

0:16–0:20 RIGHT GOES: A green arrow appears above the red car. The blue car waits patiently, the red car drives safely through. Final on-screen recap card: '1) Stop completely  2) First to stop, first to go  3) Same time? Right goes first.' Voiceover closes: 'Stop completely. First to stop goes first. Same time? The car on the right goes first.'

Visual rules: red STOP signs clearly readable. White stop lines clear. Only the cars in the script — no extra traffic, no pedestrians. Blue car = learner. Red car = car on the right. Green arrows only for the car with right of way. All movement slow, safe, realistic. Cars come to fully visible complete stops.

Negative prompt: no rolling stops, no honking, no accidents, no extra cars, no pedestrians, no cyclists, no emergency vehicles, no aggressive driving, no nighttime, no rain, no misspelled signs, no garbled text.
lessons.car-l3-speed:
Create a realistic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching FLORIDA SPEED LIMITS. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm friendly American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Aerial shot over a Florida road with palm trees. Title fades in: 'Florida Speed Limits — Default Rules'. Voiceover: 'When no sign tells you otherwise, Florida sets these default speed limits.'

0:04–0:08 SCHOOL ZONE 20: Cut to a quiet residential street with a clearly readable pentagonal yellow-green SCHOOL ZONE sign and a '20 MPH WHEN FLASHING' plate beneath it. Big on-screen number: '20 MPH'. Subtitle: 'School zone, when flashing.' Voiceover: 'Twenty miles per hour in a school zone when the lights are flashing.'

0:08–0:12 RESIDENTIAL 30: Cut to a quiet Florida residential street with mailboxes and palm trees. Big on-screen number: '30 MPH'. Subtitle: 'Residential / business district default.' Voiceover: 'Thirty miles per hour in residential and business areas, by default.'

0:12–0:16 RURAL 55: Cut to a two-lane rural Florida highway with pines and pastures. Big on-screen number: '55 MPH'. Subtitle: 'Rural roads, by default.' Voiceover: 'Fifty-five miles per hour on rural roads when no sign is posted.'

0:16–0:20 INTERSTATE 70: Cut to a clean shot of a Florida interstate sign and three lanes of light traffic. Big on-screen number: '70 MPH'. Subtitle: 'Florida interstates, when posted.' Final recap card: '20 school · 30 residential · 55 rural · 70 interstate.' Voiceover closes: 'Up to seventy on interstates where posted. Always obey the sign in front of you.'

Visual rules: numbers are huge, white on a soft dark band, perfectly spelled. Roads look clean and Florida-appropriate. No speeding visuals, no aggressive cuts.

Negative prompt: no cars exceeding the limit shown, no misspelled signs, no accidents, no police chases, no nighttime, no extra traffic, no pedestrians, no garbled text.
lessons.car-l4-dui:
Create a serious but non-graphic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching FLORIDA DUI BAC LIMITS. Style: realistic, clean, educational, calm and somber but hopeful, bright daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm serious American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Slow push-in on a clean closed Florida driver handbook on a wood table with a glass of water beside it (water only, no alcohol). Title fades in: 'Florida DUI Limits.' Voiceover: 'Florida sets clear blood-alcohol limits. Here is what you have to know.'

0:04–0:09 ADULT 0.08: Animated infographic on a soft white background — a clean rounded badge with the number '0.08%' large and centered, label below: 'Driver age 21 or older.' Voiceover: 'For drivers twenty-one and over, the legal limit is point zero eight percent.'

0:09–0:14 UNDER 21 ZERO TOLERANCE: New badge fades in with '0.02%' large and centered, label below: 'Driver under 21 — Zero Tolerance.' Voiceover: 'For drivers under twenty-one, Florida has a zero-tolerance rule. Just point zero two percent suspends your license.'

0:14–0:18 CDL 0.04: New badge fades in with '0.04%' large and centered, label below: 'Commercial driver (CDL).' Voiceover: 'For commercial drivers, the limit is point zero four percent.'

0:18–0:20 CLOSING: All three badges tile together with a final card: 'If you drink, do not drive. Plan a ride.' Voiceover closes: 'If you drink, do not drive. Plan a ride.'

Visual rules: NO alcohol, NO bottles, NO glasses of beer or wine, NO bar settings ever shown. NO traffic stops, NO police, NO crashes. The whole clip is calm, badge-style instructional graphics with the closed handbook bookending it. Numbers are huge, perfectly spelled, with the percent sign visible.

Negative prompt: no alcohol, no bottles, no glasses of beer or wine, no bars, no parties, no people drunk, no police, no sirens, no flashing lights, no traffic stops, no crashes, no nighttime, no graphic content, no misspelled numbers.
lessons.car-l5-emergency:
Create a realistic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching the FLORIDA MOVE-OVER LAW. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, smooth cinematic camera with overhead views, 16:9.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Aerial shot of a sunny Florida highway with a wide right shoulder. A Florida Highway Patrol cruiser and a tow truck are parked on the shoulder with red, blue, and amber lights flashing. Title fades in: 'Florida Move-Over Law.' Voiceover: 'When you see flashing lights on the shoulder, the law tells you exactly what to do.'

0:04–0:11 MOVE OVER ONE LANE: A blue car approaches in the right lane. A clean overhead arrow guides it to merge LEFT into the next lane, leaving the right lane completely empty next to the emergency vehicles. The car safely crosses one lane to the left. On-screen text: 'Move OVER one lane away from the emergency vehicles.' Voiceover: 'On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, you must move one lane away from the emergency vehicles.'

0:11–0:17 SLOW DOWN: New scene on a two-lane highway where moving over is unsafe. A blue car approaches and clearly slows from 55 to 35 mph. A small speedometer in the corner ticks down. On-screen text: 'Cannot move over? Slow to 20 mph BELOW the limit.' Voiceover: 'If you cannot safely move over, slow down to twenty miles per hour below the posted speed limit.'

0:17–0:20 RECAP: Final card on a clean white background: 'Move over OR slow down. Every time. By Florida law.' Voiceover closes: 'Move over, or slow down. Every time, by Florida law.'

Visual rules: blue car = the learner. Police cruiser and tow truck are parked safely on the shoulder, lights flashing, both stationary. Use overhead arrows to make the lane change crystal clear. Slow down scene shows speedometer ticking down naturally.

Negative prompt: no accidents, no honking, no aggressive lane changes, no cars hitting the emergency vehicles, no pedestrians on the shoulder, no nighttime, no rain, no extra traffic, no misspelled signs.
lessons.car-l6-perm:
Create a realistic 20-second DMV driving lesson video teaching FLORIDA LEARNER'S PERMIT RULES. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm friendly American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Hero close-up of a generic plastic learner's permit ID card lying on a clean wooden desk next to the closed Florida driver handbook. Title fades in: 'Florida Learner's Permit Rules.' Voiceover: 'Here is exactly what your Florida learner's permit lets you do.'

0:04–0:09 SUPERVISED ONLY: Animated illustration on a soft background — a clean line-art image of a learner driver and a parent in the front seats of a car, with a label arrow pointing to the front passenger seat: 'Licensed driver age 21+.' On-screen text: 'Always drive with a licensed driver 21+ in the front seat.' Voiceover: 'You must always drive with a licensed driver age twenty-one or older in the front passenger seat.'

0:09–0:14 FIRST 3 MONTHS DAYLIGHT ONLY: A simple animated sun icon and clock face appear. On-screen text: 'First 3 months: daylight hours only.' Voiceover: 'For the first three months you may only drive during daylight hours.'

0:14–0:18 AFTER 3 MONTHS UNTIL 10PM: The clock hands move forward and a moon icon fades in next to a 10:00 label. On-screen text: 'After 3 months: until 10 PM.' Voiceover: 'After three months, you may drive until ten p.m.'

0:18–0:20 RECAP: Final card: 'Permit = supervised driving. Build hours, then take the road test.' Voiceover closes: 'Build your hours, drive supervised, and you will be ready for the road test.'

Visual rules: ID card is generic — NO real names, NO real photos, NO readable license number. Use clean infographic style icons. No actual road driving in this clip — it is desk-and-icon style.

Negative prompt: no real personal information on the card, no readable license numbers, no other passengers in the car, no nighttime driving by the learner, no unsupervised teen driver, no accidents, no misspelled text.
lessons.mc-l1-gear:
Create a realistic 20-second motorcycle safety lesson video teaching the ATGATT principle — All The Gear, All The Time — for Florida motorcyclists. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic hero product shots, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm confident American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Slow push-in on a parked sport-style motorcycle in a sunny Florida driveway. Title fades in: 'ATGATT — All The Gear, All The Time.' Voiceover: 'Real riders gear up — all the gear, all the time. ATGATT.'

0:04–0:08 HELMET: Cut to a hero close-up of a black DOT-approved full-face helmet on a clean concrete surface, the bike blurred in background. On-screen text: 'DOT-approved helmet.' Voiceover: 'A D-O-T approved full-face helmet protects your head and your face.'

0:08–0:12 EYE PROTECTION: Cut to a clean shot of a clear motorcycle face shield and riding sunglasses laid side by side. On-screen text: 'Eye protection — shield or shatter-resistant glasses.' Voiceover: 'Florida law requires eye protection — a shield or shatter-resistant glasses.'

0:12–0:17 BODY GEAR: Cut to a flat lay of an armored riding jacket, riding gloves, long armored pants, and over-the-ankle boots arranged neatly on the concrete. On-screen text: 'Jacket. Gloves. Pants. Over-the-ankle boots.' Voiceover: 'Cover every limb. Armored jacket, gloves, long pants, and over-the-ankle boots.'

0:17–0:20 RECAP: Final card with all gear pieces tiled and the line: 'Dress for the slide, not the ride.' Voiceover closes: 'Dress for the slide, not the ride. Every ride.'

Visual rules: NO rider in motion in this clip — it is hero product shots of the gear itself. The motorcycle is parked the whole time. Faces are never shown. Background is sunny Florida driveway with palm trees softly out of focus.

Negative prompt: no riding, no motion of the bike, no rider on the bike, no faces, no shorts, no flip-flops, no t-shirts on a rider, no helmetless riders, no crashes, no nighttime, no rain, no logos.
lessons.mc-l2-controls:
Create a realistic 20-second motorcycle lesson video teaching the FOUR PRIMARY CONTROLS of a motorcycle. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic close-ups of a parked motorcycle, 16:9.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide static shot of a parked clean standard motorcycle in a sunny Florida driveway. Title fades in: 'Knowing the Controls — Right hand, left hand, right foot, left foot.' Voiceover: 'A motorcycle uses all four limbs. Here is what each one does.'

0:04–0:08 RIGHT HAND: Cut to extreme close-up of a gloved right hand resting on the right grip — throttle and front brake. On-screen text: 'RIGHT HAND — Throttle + Front Brake.' Voiceover: 'Your right hand controls the throttle and the front brake.'

0:08–0:12 LEFT HAND: Cut to extreme close-up of a gloved left hand resting on the left grip — clutch lever. On-screen text: 'LEFT HAND — Clutch.' Voiceover: 'Your left hand pulls the clutch lever to change gears.'

0:12–0:16 RIGHT FOOT: Cut to extreme close-up of a riding boot on the right peg above the rear brake pedal. On-screen text: 'RIGHT FOOT — Rear Brake.' Voiceover: 'Your right foot presses the rear brake.'

0:16–0:20 LEFT FOOT: Cut to extreme close-up of a riding boot on the left peg above the gear shifter. On-screen text: 'LEFT FOOT — Gear Shift.' Final recap card: 'Four limbs. Four controls. One smooth ride.' Voiceover closes: 'Your left foot shifts gears. Four limbs, four controls. Master them and you will ride smooth.'

Visual rules: motorcycle is parked, static, never moving. Camera holds steady on each control with gentle slight push-in. No rider visible above the gloves and boots. No face.

Negative prompt: no riding, no motion of the bike, no face, no other vehicles, no people, no aggressive twist of the throttle, no readable instrument panel text other than the captions specified.
lessons.mc-l3-corner:
Create a realistic 20-second motorcycle lesson video teaching the SLOW-LOOK-PRESS-ROLL cornering technique. Style: realistic, clean, educational, golden afternoon Florida light on a quiet country road, smooth cinematic camera, 16:9.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide cinematic shot of an empty sweeping curve on a Florida country road lined with palms, no traffic. Title fades in: 'Cornering — Slow, Look, Press, Roll.' Voiceover: 'Every safe corner uses the same four-step technique.'

0:04–0:08 SLOW: A single motorcycle (rider helmeted, no face shown) approaches the curve, sitting upright, clearly slowing down before the turn. On-screen text: '1. SLOW — before the turn.' Voiceover: 'First, slow down before you enter the corner.'

0:08–0:12 LOOK: Close-up of the helmeted rider's head turning to look through the corner toward the exit. On-screen text: '2. LOOK — through the turn to where you want to go.' Voiceover: 'Second, look where you want to go, all the way through the turn.'

0:12–0:16 PRESS: Mid-shot of the motorcycle leaning gracefully into the apex of the curve, gloved hand visibly pressing forward on the inside grip. On-screen text: '3. PRESS — inside grip to lean the bike.' Voiceover: 'Third, press the inside grip to make the bike lean and steer through the curve.'

0:16–0:20 ROLL: The motorcycle exits the corner, leaning back to upright, and smoothly rolls on the throttle into the straight ahead. On-screen text: '4. ROLL — on the throttle out.' Final recap card: 'Slow. Look. Press. Roll.' Voiceover closes: 'Slow. Look. Press. Roll. Every corner, every time.'

Visual rules: only one motorcycle in frame. No oncoming traffic. Rider faces never shown — back of helmet only. Smooth, controlled riding the entire time.

Negative prompt: no crashes, no skidding, no other vehicles, no oncoming traffic in the lane, no aggressive lean angles, no face, no readable license plate, no bicycles, no pedestrians, no rain, no nighttime.
lessons.mc-l4-fl-law:
Create a realistic 20-second motorcycle lesson video teaching FLORIDA MOTORCYCLE LAW basics. Style: realistic, clean, educational, bright Florida daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm confident American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Aerial shot of a sunny Florida coastal highway with a single motorcycle riding cleanly in the right lane. Title fades in: 'Florida Motorcycle Law.' Voiceover: 'Three Florida laws every rider must know.'

0:04–0:09 HELMET LAW: Hero shot of a black DOT-approved full-face helmet on a parked motorcycle. On-screen text: 'Riders under 21: Helmet REQUIRED. 21+: required unless $10,000 medical insurance.' Voiceover: 'Riders under twenty-one must always wear a D-O-T helmet. Riders twenty-one and over must wear one unless they carry at least ten thousand dollars in medical insurance.'

0:09–0:14 LANE SHARING: Aerial overhead view of two motorcycles riding side by side LEGALLY in the same single lane on a Florida road. On-screen text: 'Two motorcycles MAY share one lane. NO splitting between cars.' Voiceover: 'Two motorcycles can legally share one lane. Lane splitting between cars is illegal in Florida.'

0:14–0:18 HEADLIGHT ON: Hero close-up of a parked motorcycle with its headlight glowing brightly in midday sunlight. On-screen text: 'Headlight ON, day and night.' Voiceover: 'Your headlight must be on any time the motorcycle is in use, day and night.'

0:18–0:20 RECAP: Final card with three icons: helmet, two-bikes-in-lane, headlight. Text: 'Helmet. Lane share. Headlight ON.' Voiceover closes: 'Helmet up, share the lane, headlight on. Ride legal in Florida.'

Visual rules: motorcycles are clean and modern. Riders' faces never shown — back of helmet only. Lane share scene clearly shows two bikes IN the same lane, NOT between cars.

Negative prompt: no lane splitting between cars, no helmetless under-21 riders, no crashes, no faces, no readable license plates, no aggressive riding, no rain, no nighttime, no other vehicles in the lane-share scene.
lessons.cdl-l1-pretrip:
Create a realistic 20-second CDL training video teaching the SEVEN-STEP PRE-TRIP WALK-AROUND of a semi-truck. Style: realistic, clean, professional, bright Florida daylight, smooth cinematic camera, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm authoritative American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide static shot of a clean parked Florida-plated semi-truck on a bright morning. Title fades in: 'Pre-Trip Inspection — 7 Steps.' Voiceover: 'A safe trip starts with a complete walk-around. Seven steps, every time.'

0:04–0:07 STEP 1 FRONT: Cut to a front-three-quarter view of the truck cab. Caption: '1. Front of cab — lights, wipers, windshield.' Voiceover: 'One. The front of the cab.'

0:07–0:10 STEP 2 ENGINE: Cut to the open engine bay with the hood tilted forward. Caption: '2. Engine compartment — belts, hoses, fluids.' Voiceover: 'Two. The engine compartment.'

0:10–0:12 STEP 3 STEERING: Cut to a low-angle shot of the front axle and steering linkage. Caption: '3. Front suspension & steering.' Voiceover: 'Three. Front suspension and steering.'

0:12–0:14 STEP 4 CAB INTERIOR: Cut to interior dashboard and gauges. Caption: '4. Inside cab — gauges, belts, mirrors.' Voiceover: 'Four. Inside the cab.'

0:14–0:16 STEP 5 SIDE: Cut to a side tracking shot down the truck body. Caption: '5. Driver side — fuel tank, drive shaft, batteries.' Voiceover: 'Five. The driver side.'

0:16–0:18 STEP 6 COUPLING: Cut to a close-up of the fifth wheel, kingpin, and air/electrical hoses. Caption: '6. Coupling system.' Voiceover: 'Six. The coupling system.'

0:18–0:20 STEP 7 REAR: Cut to a clean rear shot showing brake lights, mud flaps, doors. Caption: '7. Rear of trailer — lights, doors, mud flaps.' Final recap card: '7 Steps. Every Trip.' Voiceover closes: 'Seven. The rear. Every step, every trip.'

Visual rules: truck is clean, parked, never moving. NO driver visible. Each step shot is steady, mechanical-detail focus. Captions are large and perfectly spelled.

Negative prompt: no driver in frame, no people, no truck moving, no other vehicles, no rain, no nighttime, no readable secondary text, no garbled signage, no extra clutter.
lessons.cdl-l2-airbrakes:
Create a realistic 20-second CDL training video teaching AIR BRAKES FUNDAMENTALS. Style: realistic, clean, professional, mechanical close-ups, bright daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm authoritative American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide shot of a parked clean semi-truck with focus on the rear axle area. Title fades in: 'Air Brakes 101.' Voiceover: 'Every CDL driver must know the air brake basics.'

0:04–0:09 COMPRESSOR + GAUGE: Cut to a hero close-up of a stylized truck dashboard air-pressure gauge. The needle climbs smoothly from 60 psi past 100 psi. Caption: 'Compressor builds air pressure. Normal: 100–125 psi.' Voiceover: 'The compressor builds air pressure. Normal operating range is one hundred to one hundred twenty-five p-s-i.'

0:09–0:14 LOW-AIR WARNING: Cut to a stylized dashboard with a red LOW AIR warning light pulsing next to a gauge dropping toward 55 psi. Caption: 'Below 60 psi: LOW AIR warning. Pull over safely.' Voiceover: 'Below sixty p-s-i, the low-air warning activates. Pull over safely.'

0:14–0:18 SPRING BRAKE POPS: Cut to a yellow octagonal spring-brake parking knob popping out automatically on the dashboard. Caption: 'Below 20–45 psi: spring brakes engage automatically.' Voiceover: 'If pressure keeps falling, the spring brakes pop out and lock the wheels automatically.'

0:18–0:20 RECAP: Final card: 'Build air. Watch the gauge. Heed the warning.' Voiceover closes: 'Build air, watch the gauge, heed the warning.'

Visual rules: gauges are clean, perfectly readable, with the needle motion smooth and obvious. Yellow octagonal knob is the standard CDL parking brake control. NO driver visible.

Negative prompt: no driver in frame, no people, no truck moving, no crashes, no smoke, no fire, no garbled gauge numerals, no extra clutter, no logos.
lessons.cdl-l3-disqual:
Create a serious but non-graphic 20-second CDL training video teaching CDL DISQUALIFICATIONS. Style: realistic, clean, professional, calm and serious mood, bright daylight, cinematic, 16:9. Voiceover is a calm serious American instructor.

0:00–0:04 OPENING: Wide static shot of a parked clean semi-truck cab in a quiet truck-stop lot. Title fades in: 'CDL Disqualifications — Don't Lose Your License.' Voiceover: 'Some violations end a CDL career. Here is what every driver must know.'

0:04–0:09 FIRST MAJOR — 1 YEAR: Animated infographic on a soft background — large badge: '1 YEAR' with subtext: 'First major offense (DUI, refusal, leaving scene, felony in vehicle).' Voiceover: 'A first major offense — like D-U-I, refusing a test, leaving the scene, or a felony involving the vehicle — disqualifies you for one year.'

0:09–0:14 SECOND MAJOR — LIFETIME: New badge fades in: 'LIFETIME' with subtext: 'Second major offense.' Voiceover: 'A second major offense disqualifies you for life.'

0:14–0:18 SERIOUS — 60/120 DAYS: New badge fades in: '60 / 120 DAYS' with subtext: 'Serious traffic violations: 2nd in 3 yrs = 60 days. 3rd = 120 days.' Voiceover: 'Two serious traffic violations in three years means sixty days off. Three means one hundred twenty days.'

0:18–0:20 RECAP: Final card: 'Drive professional. Protect your CDL. Protect your career.' Voiceover closes: 'Drive professional. Protect your CDL.'

Visual rules: all-infographic animation. NO depiction of crashes, NO police, NO actual violations. The truck appears only at the open and close. Calm somber tone. Numbers and labels are huge and perfectly spelled.

Negative prompt: no crashes, no police, no traffic stops, no alcohol, no flashing lights, no nighttime, no graphic content, no people in distress, no garbled text, no misspelled numbers.
